reviews.title: Delicious experience in the restaurant Alegria - what a delicious piuran food!
reviews.text: On January 19th my husband and I and family went to lunch to say goodbye to Peru after having spent 1 month on vacation and returning to Switzerland where we live.  The very very warm welcome as are the puruan people, the frame, the place, decoration and atmosphere very cheerful worth the redundancy! We were greeted with a shot of warm tiger milk or something very complimentary with chiffons. We had in the group of 7, my 2 little 4 nephews and a 20 month old baby and we got a nice table on the terrace and a chair for the baby. The George took care of us wonderfully. His explanations about the dishes put water in our mouths and the final result exceeded our expectations. The picadito picantero, dry Chabelo and majado de yuca I loved! ; the classic sebiche with the fishing of the day not to mention, the wood-fired octopus macerated in chicha de jora and jíes for 24 hours will remain in our taste memory for a long time! And the duck stew with pepian how rich! Pure fish chick no longer! And when it came to ordering drinks the cocktails of La Alegria (its improved version of pisco sour) made us even more joyful! Don't have purple chicha or lemonade on the menu but they weren't missed because the coconut water in their own coconut, the mango plum soda, the barley and the tamarind water were more than fine!  As for desserts, we only ordered the reinvented 3-star pionono with coconut ice cream and carobine honey. There were other rich options but we no longer had space! Although for a delicious complimentary carobine cocktail! Anyway we will return on our next trip to Peru to try other exquisite dishes and desserts! I highly recommend this restaurant of piuran food that as the name suggests left me that feeling of Alegria and the pride of being Peruvian. How delicious is eaten in Peru and this time the piuran food came to my soul!
